title: Vectors: Column Vectors and Vector Geometry
description: Add, subtract and scale column vectors, find magnitudes, and use position vectors, ratios and parallel-vector tests for collinearity and velocity questions (Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended).

notes.heading: Column Vectors and Their Components
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A vector has both size and direction. At IGCSE we write vectors as columns, for example

$$\mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$$

The top component counts how far right (left is negative) and the bottom counts how far up (down is negative). AB means 'the vector from A to B'.

notes.heading: Adding Vectors
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Add matching components:

$$\begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} c \\ d \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a + c \\ b + d \end{pmatrix}$$

🔑 How it works
Addition follows the triangle law: 'from A to B, then from B to C' gives AC = AB + BC. Two vectors are equal only when both components match.

💡 Worked Example
$\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ + $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$.

notes.heading: Subtracting: the Vector from A to B
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Subtract matching components, and remember:

$$\vec{{AB}} = \vec{{OB}} - \vec{{OA}}$$

🔑 How it works
AB answers 'how do I get from A to B?' - destination minus start. Reversing a vector negates it: BA = -AB. The classic slip is writing OA - OB, which points the wrong way.

💡 Worked Example
OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and OB = $\begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ give AB = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

notes.heading: Scalar Multiplication and Magnitude
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Multiplying a vector by the scalar k scales every component by k; a negative k reverses the direction. The magnitude comes from Pythagoras:

$$\lvert \mathbf{a} \rvert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \text{ for } \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$$

💡 Worked Example
3 $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 15 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$, and the magnitude of $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ is $\sqrt{9 + 16}$ = 5.

notes.heading: Parallel Vectors are Scalar Multiples
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Two vectors are parallel exactly when one is a scalar multiple of the other: a = k b.

🔑 How it works
Both components must give the SAME k. A negative k still means parallel - just in the opposite direction.

💡 Worked Example
$\begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ = -2 x $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$ because -2 x 2 = -4 and -2 x -3 = 6, so the vectors are parallel with k = -2.

notes.heading: Position Vectors: Midpoints, Ratios and Collinearity
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The position vector of a point is the vector from the origin to it. The midpoint of A and B has position vector (OA + OB) / 2, and a point P with AP : PB = 2 : 1 has OP = OA + (2/3) AB.

🔑 How it works
For ratio m : n travel the fraction m / (m + n) of the way along AB. To prove A, B and C collinear, show AB is a scalar multiple of AC - and state that the two segments share point A.

💡 Worked Example
A(1, 2), B(7, 8): AB = $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$, AP = (2/3) x $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$, so OP = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$.

notes.heading: Velocity is a Vector
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Velocity carries direction as well as size, so displacement = velocity x time, component by component.

🔑 How it works
When two motions act together - a boat and a current - add the velocity vectors first. Multiply by whole seconds.

💡 Worked Example
Velocity $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s for 5 s gives displacement $\begin{pmatrix} 15 \\ -20 \end{pmatrix}$ m, a distance of 5 x $\sqrt{9 + 16}$ = 25 m from the start.

flashcards.definition: Top component: how far right. Bottom component: how far up.
AB = OB - OA: destination minus start.
Multiply every component by k; negative k reverses direction.
One vector is a scalar multiple of the other, with the same k on both components.
The vector from the origin O to the point.
Half the sum of the two position vectors.
OP = OA + (2/3) AB - travel two-thirds of the way.
AB is a scalar multiple of AC (or BC), and the segments share a point.
Multiply the velocity vector by the time.
flashcards.example: Velocity $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s for 5 s gives $\begin{pmatrix} 15 \\ -20 \end{pmatrix}$ m

questions.explanation: Multiply BOTH components by 3: 3 x 5 = 15 and 3 x -2 = -6. The bottom is easy to forget.
Pythagoras: sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5. (25 is the square, not the length.)

questions.stem: The vector $\begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ is a scalar multiple of $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$. What is the scalar?
questions.explanation: -2 x $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ (check both components: -2 x 2 = -4 and -2 x -3 = 6). The vectors are parallel but point the opposite way.

questions.stem: With respect to origin O, OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and OB = $\begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Find AB.
questions.explanation: AB = OB - OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$. Destination minus start; $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$ is the reverse vector BA.

questions.stem: a = $\begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$ and b = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$. Work out a - b.
questions.explanation: -3 - 4 = -7 for the top, and 5 - (-2) = 7 for the bottom. Watch the double negative.

questions.stem: A has position vector $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$ and B has position vector $\begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$. Find the position vector of the midpoint of AB.
A = $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ and B = $\begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix}$ are position vectors. P lies on AB with AP : PB = 2 : 1. Find the position vector of P.
questions.explanation: AB = $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$, AP = (2/3) x $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$, so OP = $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ + $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$. (4,4 is AP, not the position vector.)

questions.stem: A particle moves with constant velocity $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s. How far is it from its starting point after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: Displacement = 5 x $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 15 \\ -20 \end{pmatrix}$ m, and its magnitude is sqrt(15^2 + 20^2) = 25 m - or 5 s x 5 m/s speed.

questions.stem: In triangle OAB, M is the midpoint of AB. OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ and OB = $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$. Find OM.
questions.explanation: OM = (OA + OB) / 2 = $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ / 2 = $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Subtracting first instead gives the (1,4) trap.

questions.stem: OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$, OB = $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix}$ and OC = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 14 \end{pmatrix}$ are position vectors, and A, B and C lie on a straight line. Which statement shows this?
questions.explanation: AB = $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ and AC = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 12 \end{pmatrix}$ = 2 x $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$. One vector being a scalar multiple of the other, sharing point A, proves collinearity.

questions.stem: OA = $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ and OB = $\begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 15 \end{pmatrix}$ are position vectors. C lies on AB with AC : CB = 1 : 2. Find the position vector of C.
The vector $\begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ k \end{pmatrix}$ has magnitude 17, where k is positive. Find k.
questions.explanation: k^2 = 17^2 - 8^2 = 289 - 64 = 225, so k = 15 - the 8, 15, 17 Pythagorean triple.

questions.stem: A boat sails with velocity $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s in still water while the current flows at $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s. What is the magnitude of the boat's actual velocity?
questions.explanation: Resultant velocity = $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ + $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ = $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ m/s, magnitude sqrt(25 + 1) = $\sqrt{26}$ m/s (about 5.1 m/s).
